history.p: Hartmann wrote his overture to Adam Oehlenschläger's tragedy "Hakon Jarl" in 1844. The incidental music was written for the revival of the play in 1857, but Hartmann chose to give it the same opus number as the overture.

physDesc.physMedium: In leather half-binding with marbled sides. Handwritten label in Hartmann's hand on front cover, inscribed: "3 Mellemacter til / Tragedien 'Hakon Jarl' / Partitur". On the verso of the title page written in pencil in foreign hand: "No I und III aber in folgender Partiturordnung: Flauti / Oboi / Clar. / Fag. / Corni / Corn. / Trombe / Tromboni / Timpani / Viol 1. / Viol. 2 / Viola / Cello / Basso". This was probably added in connection with the performance in Leipzig on 10 February 1876, when Carl Reinecke asked for Hartmann's permission to make a personal copy of the score, which is notated in the old fashioned way with the strings at top. Paginated 2-37. On p. 98, bars cancelled. At the end of the music on p. 37 signed and end-dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann / 18 Marts 1857."

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in brown library binding. On the spine printed in gold, the monogram of King Christian X and: "J.P.E. / Hartmann / Hakon / Jarl / Ouverture / og / Mellemakts- / musik." Written in black ink. Paper: 20 staves. On the second title page, the following has been cancelled: "Ouverture / til Tragedien / 'Hakon Jarl' / componeret og / 'Hakon Jarls' udødelige Forfatter tilegnet / af I.P.E. Hartmann / Op. 40." and "Hedenskabets Kamp i Norge med Christendommen / og dennes Seir ved Olaf Trygvason. / Kampf des Heidenthums in Norwegen gegen den Christenthum, und Sieg der letzten durch Olaf Trygvason" written in pencil in Hartmann's hand. Overture and incidental music paginated separately. Last two pages blank. On the first music page, notes for the copyist: "NB: "Die Instrumenten müssen in der angegeben Ordnung gestellt werden", which is indicated by figures in red crayon.
Bound in brown paper. Stamped "Det Kgl. Theaters Musikarkiv". Contains also parts for the "Hakon Jarl Overture" (HartW 33).
